summary: Moldova keeps a broad visa-free list — EU/EFTA, the US, UK, Canada, Japan, the Western Balkans, most CIS countries and much of Latin America get 90 days in any 180-day period — while most other nationalities can apply online for an eVisa through the official evisa.gov.md portal.

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of Bahrain, Belize, Bolivia, Cambodia, Cabo Verde, China, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Fiji, Gabon, Guyana, Haiti, India, Jamaica, Kuwait, Madagascar, the Maldives, Mongolia, Nauru, Oman, Papua New Guinea, São Tomé and Príncipe, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Eswatini, Thailand, Comoros and Togo who hold a valid residence permit or visa (not a transit visa) issued by an EU or Schengen state, the UK, the US or Canada can travel to Moldova without a visa while that permit or visa is valid.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Integration of Moldova — Visa regime for foreigners

fee.notes: Stated by the eVisa portal; paid by card when the online application is complete. Some applicants may need an invitation or supporting documents.

source.name: 10 lucruri pe care trebuie sa le cunoşti despre serviciul eVisa

fee.notes: Issued by Moldovan diplomatic missions where the eVisa is unavailable or a multiple-entry visa is needed. Confirm the current fee with the mission.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Integration of Moldova — Types of visas and requirements

fee.notes: For stays over 90 days — work, study, family reunification — followed by a residence permit in Moldova. Confirm the current fee and documents with the Moldovan mission.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Integration of Moldova — Types of visas and requirements

passportValidity.text: On the day you enter, your passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond the date you are due to leave Moldova, and it must have been issued within the last 10 years.

source.name: Border Police of the Republic of Moldova — Border crossing by foreign citizens
Border Police of the Republic of Moldova — Border crossing by foreign citizens

travelInsurance.text: Visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance valid throughout Moldova for the whole stay, covering medical repatriation, emergency treatment and hospitalization, of at least €30,000. No insurance is checked for visa-free entry, but cover is strongly recommended for all visitors.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Integration of Moldova — Types of visas and requirements

onwardTicket.text: Moldovan law lists a return or round-trip ticket among the documents a tourist may be asked to show to justify the visit, together with proof of accommodation and of enough money for the stay and the journey home or onward.

source.name: Border Police of the Republic of Moldova — Border crossing by foreign citizens

proofOfFunds.text: Every foreigner must be able to show adequate means both to live on during the stay and to return home or travel on, together with documents that justify the purpose of the trip, such as a hotel booking or a host's invitation.

source.name: Border Police of the Republic of Moldova — Border crossing by foreign citizens

currencyLimits.text: Cash of more than €10,000 (or equivalent) must be declared in writing when entering or leaving Moldova; larger sums may require supporting bank documents to take out.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Integration of Moldova — Customs rules

notes: The UK FCDO says you must get permission from the Moldovan Department of Monuments to take any artwork or antiques out of the country; otherwise customs can seize them and you could face criminal charges.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says paying by card is now generally widespread, though not always possible, particularly outside Chișinău; US dollars and euros are the most widely accepted foreign currencies, and notes should be in perfect condition. Foreign cards do not work at banks in Transnistria, which uses its own Transnistrian ruble.

safety.text: Moldova is generally safe with low violent crime; petty theft occurs in Chișinău. The UK advises against all travel to the breakaway Transnistria region, which is outside government control, and the war in neighboring Ukraine means advisories can change. Check them before travel.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Moldova travel advice

roadVignette.appliesTo: Vehicles NOT registered in Moldova, and their trailers, that enter or transit the country — cars fall under tariff heading 8703.
roadVignette.text: Moldova's vignette is a road-use charge on foreign-registered vehicles: if your car was not registered in Moldova, you need one to drive anywhere in the country, not just on main roads, and a towed trailer needs its own. Buy it online before you reach the border. Diplomatic vehicles and holders of a "tax exempt" international transport permit do not pay it.

idp.text: Moldova is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Moldova is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Moldova yet.

tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Transnistria, which is outside the control of the Moldovan government. At the de facto checkpoints passports are checked but not stamped, and you must fill in a migration card and keep a copy to show when you leave. All crossings between Ukraine and Transnistria are temporarily closed.

If you enter Moldova overland from Ukraine, the UK FCDO says to use an internationally recognised crossing point in the north or south of the country, outside the Transnistria region. Check the Moldovan Border Police for updates before you travel.
The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and only a few ATMs in Chișinău accept foreign cards. Lei are not accepted in Transnistria, and foreign cards do not work there.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Moldova?
faq.answer: Probably not: citizens of the EU/EFTA, US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, the Western Balkans, most CIS countries and much of Latin America can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Nationalities that do need a visa can usually apply online through the official evisa.gov.md portal.

faq.question: How do I get a Moldova eVisa?
faq.answer: Apply online at evisa.gov.md — the only official portal. Upload your passport, travel details and any required supporting documents; the fee is €40, and a decision takes up to 10 calendar days (up to 20 if the review is extended), so apply well before travel.

faq.question: Can I visit Transnistria?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Transnistria. It is outside the control of the Moldovan government, and the de facto authorities may ask the purpose of your visit or deny you entry. If you go, fill in the two-copy migration card at the checkpoint and keep one copy to show when you leave.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Moldova without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt visitors can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period. For longer stays you need a long-stay (Type D) visa and then a residence permit from the migration authorities.

faq.question: Is Moldova in the EU or the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: No — Moldova is not an EU member and is not in the Schengen Area, so days spent in Moldova do not count toward your Schengen 90-day limit.
